<img class="tool-icon" src="../../../../images/tekla/tools/urebarclassdecoder.svg" alt="" width="48" height="48" style="display:block;margin:0 0 1rem;background:#fff;border-radius:8px;padding:4px" />

{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Rebar → `uRebarClassDecoder` (also on the Comma ribbon tab)
{{% /callout %}}

Two modes, picked from the Mode dropdown at the top of the dialog. Both work the same way otherwise: run on whatever is selected in the model, or on the entire model.

| Mode | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Decode: Class → UDAs** | Reads each object's own Class (must already be set, as a 4-digit code) and writes N\_BAR\_LAYER, N\_BAR\_DIRECTION and N\_BAR\_CONDITION from it. |
| **Compile: UDAs → Class** | The reverse — reads N\_BAR\_LAYER, N\_BAR\_DIRECTION and N\_BAR\_CONDITION and writes Class from them. A UDA that was never set counts as Other (OTH, digit 9), so a bar with none of the three set compiles to 9999. |

**Class code reference.** Open *Class code reference* in the dialog to see what each digit of the code means — layer name, layer number, direction and pour condition, from the firm's MT-M-02.3 rule sheet — with worked examples and a box that decodes any 4-digit code you type. The whole one-page sheet, which also covers part classification and the bridge part names, opens from *Classification rule (PDF)* at the top right of the dialog. It is installed with the plugin, so it works without the network or the firm folder.
